method.method_draft: Assign variables to the five vertices read from the diagram: top vertex T=1, left vertex L=5, front-centre vertex F=x, right vertex R=y, and bottom vertex B=z. From the triangular-bipyramid drawing, list the six triangular faces as TLF, TFR, TRL, BLF, BFR, and BRL, where LR is the dashed hidden edge. Since all face sums are equal, write 1+5+x = 1+x+y = 1+y+5 = z+5+x = z+x+y = z+y+5. Compare the first two equations to get y=5; compare the first and third to get x=y, so x=5; compare the first and fourth to get z=1. Add all vertex numbers: 1+5+5+5+1=17.

method.method_draft: Use local cancellation between pairs of adjacent triangular faces. From the image, identify the top vertex as 1, the left vertex as 5, and the other three vertices as front-centre F, right R, and bottom B. The two top faces sharing edge top-left are TLF and TLR; equal sums imply F=R after cancelling T and L. The two top faces sharing edge top-right are TRF and TRL; equal sums imply F=L, so F=5, and hence R=5. Now compare the top and bottom faces sharing the edge left-front, namely TLF and BLF; cancelling L and F gives B=T=1. Therefore the five vertex numbers are 1, 5, 5, 5, and 1, whose sum is 17.
